en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty-Section First Chapter
The Discourse on the Holy Life;
the Discourse on the Pure Holy Life:
"Is there no dwelling in the holy life among the devas?"
“Yes.

[The opponent asks: “Are all the gods dull-witted, mute like elephants, and ignorant, communicating only by hand gestures, and incapable of understanding the meaning of well-spoken or ill-spoken words?
Are all the gods not confident in the Buddha, not confident in the Dhamma, and not confident in the Saṅgha?”
They do not wait upon the Buddha, the Blessed One; they do not question the Buddha, the Blessed One;
and when questions are answered by the Buddha, the Blessed One, they are not satisfied.

All those gods are possessed of an obstruction of karma, possessed of an obstruction of defilements, and possessed of an obstruction of maturation; they are faithless, lacking aspiration, and of poor wisdom.
They are incapable of entering into the certainty of rightness regarding wholesome states;
all those gods are matricides, patricides, murderers of arahants, shedders of blood, and schismatics of the Saṅgha;

all those gods are takers of life, takers of what is not given, practitioners of sexual misconduct, speakers of falsehood, speakers of divisive speech, speakers of harsh speech, idle chatterers, and covetous.
"Are they malevolent in mind and of wrong view?
"One should not say so... [and so on].

"Is it not the case that there are gods who are not dull-witted, not deaf-mute, but wise, who do not communicate by hand-signs, and are capable of discerning what is well-spoken and what is ill-spoken?"
It is possible to understand this: there are deities who have confidence in the Buddha, confidence in the Dhamma, and confidence in the Saṅgha;
they attend upon the Blessed Buddha, they question the Blessed Buddha, and when their questions are answered by the Blessed Buddha, they are uplifted in mind.
There are deities who are not possessed of an obstruction of karma, nor possessed of an obstruction of defilements.
Those endowed with faith, zeal, and wisdom, though possessed of the obstruction of karmic fruition, are capable of entering into the certainty of rightness regarding wholesome states.
There are gods who are not matricides, not patricides, not murderers of Arhats, not shedders of blood [of an Arhat], and not schismatics of the Saṅgha;
there are gods who do not take life and do not take what is not given.
Are they not those who engage in sexual misconduct, nor speak falsehoods, nor speak maliciously, nor speak harshly, nor indulge in idle chatter;
nor are they covetous, nor malevolent in heart, but rather possess right view?
Yes, they are.

If there are gods who are not dull-witted, not deaf-mute, wise, not communicating by hand gestures, and capable of understanding the meaning of what is well-spoken and what is ill-spoken … [and so on] … if there are gods who have confidence in the Buddha … [and so on] … who possess right view,
then indeed, sir, it should not be said: [that there are no such beings].
“There is no living of the holy life among the devas.
Is there a living of the holy life among the devas? Yes.

Is there there the going forth, the shaving of the head, the wearing of the saffron robes, and the carrying of the bowl? Do perfectly enlightened Buddhas arise among the devas? Do paccekabuddhas arise? Does a pair of chief disciples arise?
You should not say so… [as before]… If there is no going forth among the devas, is it not the case that there is no living of the holy life (brahmacariya) among the devas?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Is it the case that wherever there is going forth (pabbajjā), there alone is the life of purity (brahmacariyavāsa), and wherever there is no going forth, there is no life of purity?
You should not speak thus …pe…
Is it the case that wherever there is going forth, there alone is the living of the holy life (brahmacariya), and wherever there is no going forth, there is no living of the holy life?
Yes. Is it the case that only for one who goes forth is there the living of the holy life, and for one who does not go forth there is no living of the holy life?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … “There is no shaving of the head among the devas,” does it follow that “there is no living the holy life (brahmacariya) among the devas”? Yes.

"Is it the case that wherever there is shaving of the head, there alone is the living of the holy life (brahmacariya), and wherever there is no shaving of the head, there is no living of the holy life?
"One should not say so... [and so on] ...
"Is it the case that wherever there is shaving of the head, there alone is the living of the holy life, and wherever there is no shaving of the head, there is no living of the holy life?"
“Yes,” you say.
“Is it only for one who is shaven that there is the living of the holy life (brahmacariya), and for one who is not shaven there is no living of the holy life?
You should not speak thus… [and so on].
Is it the case that there is no wearing of the saffron robe among the devas, and that there is no living of the holy life (brahmacariya) among the devas?
Yes, it is so.

Then, is it the case that wherever there is the wearing of the saffron robe, there alone is the living of the holy life; and wherever there is no wearing of the saffron robe, there is no living of the holy life?

It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is it the case that wherever there is the wearing of the saffron robe, there alone is the life of the holy life (brahmacariya), and wherever there is no wearing of the saffron robe, there is no life of the holy life? Yes.
"Is it the case that only he who wears the saffron robe dwells in the holy life, while for him who does not wear the saffron robe there is no dwelling in the holy life?
"One should not say so... [and so on].
"If there is no wearing of alms-bowls among the devas, is there then no dwelling in the holy life among the devas?"
“Yes,” [you say].

“Is it the case that wherever there is the wearing of alms-bowls, there alone is the living of the holy life (brahmacariya), and wherever there is no wearing of alms-bowls, there is no living of the holy life?
You should not speak thus …pe…

Is it the case that wherever there is the carrying of a bowl, there alone is the living of the holy life (brahmacariya), and wherever there is no carrying of a bowl, there is no living of the holy life?
Yes.
Is it the case that only for one who carries a bowl is there the living of the holy life, and for one who does not carry a bowl, there is no living of the holy life?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … “Perfectly Enlightened Ones do not arise among the devas; there is no living of the holy life (brahmacariya) among the devas,” is that so? Yes.
Is it the case that only where Fully Enlightened Ones arise is there a dwelling in the holy life, and where Fully Enlightened Ones do not arise, there is no dwelling in the holy life?

One should certainly not say so … [as before] … Is it the case that only where Fully Enlightened Ones arise is there a dwelling in the holy life, and where Fully Enlightened Ones do not arise, there is no dwelling in the holy life?
“Yes,” he replied.
“The Blessed One was born at Lumbinī; he attained full enlightenment at the foot of the Bodhi tree; and it was at Bārāṇasī that the Blessed One set in motion the Wheel of Dhamma.
Is it only there that the holy life is lived, and not elsewhere?”
It should not be said thus … [as before] … “Paccekabuddhas do not arise among the devas”? “There is no living of the holy life (brahmacariya) among the devas”? Yes.
Is it to be said that the holy life exists only where Paccekabuddhas arise, and that where Paccekabuddhas do not arise, there is no holy life?
One should certainly not say so...
[and so on] ... Is it to be said that the holy life exists only where Paccekabuddhas arise, and that where Paccekabuddhas do not arise, there is no holy life?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Is it the case that Pratyekabuddhas arise in the Middle Countries, and that the living of the holy life (brahmacariya) occurs only there, and not elsewhere?
You should not speak thus … [and so on] … No, you should not.
If it is accepted that a pair of disciples does not arise among the devas, then is it not the case that there is no living of the holy life (brahmacariya) among the devas?
Yes, it is.
Wherever a pair of disciples arises, there alone is the living of the holy life; wherever a pair of disciples does not arise, there is no living of the holy life. Is this so? Yes, it is.

It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is it the case that wherever a pair of disciples arises, there alone is the dwelling of the holy life (brahmacariya), and wherever a pair of disciples does not arise, there is no dwelling of the holy life?
Yes.
Is it the case that a pair of disciples has arisen among the Magadhans, and that the life of the holy life (*brahmacariya*) exists only there,
and not elsewhere? One should not say so… [and so forth]… Does the life of the holy life exist among the devas?
“Yes,” you say.
“Is there a life of purity (brahmacariya) among all the devas?
You should not speak thus … [and so on] … No.
Is there a life of purity among human beings?
Yes. Is there a life of purity among all human beings?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is there a life of purity (brahmacariya) among the devas? Yes.
Is there a dwelling in the holy life among the non-percipient beings in the deva realms?
One should not say so… [and so on] … Is there a dwelling in the holy life among human beings?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Is there a life of celibacy (*brahmacariya*) in the border regions among the barbarians who do not understand, where there is no access for monks, nuns, laymen, or laywomen?
You should not speak thus.
"Is there a dwelling in the holy life among the devas?
"There is where it exists, and there is where it does not exist.

"Among the devas who are non-percipient beings, is there a dwelling in the holy life where it exists and where it does not exist? Among the devas who are percipient beings, is there a dwelling in the holy life where it exists and where it does not exist?"
It should not be said so.
Is it the case that among the devas, there are some where the holy life (brahmacariya) is practiced and others where it is not? Yes.
Where does it exist, and where does it not exist?
It does not exist among the non-percipient beings in the deva realms; it exists among the percipient beings in the deva realms.
Does it not exist among the non-percipient beings in the deva realms?
“Yes.
“In the gods who are beings of perception, there is no living of the holy life (brahmacariya),” you must not say this.
Is there a dwelling in the holy life among the non-percipient beings in the deva realms?
Yes. Is there a dwelling in the holy life among the percipient beings in the deva realms? Yes. Is there a dwelling in the holy life among the non-percipient beings in the deva realms? No.
It should not be said so.
Is there a life of purity lived among humans?
There is where it exists; there is where it does not exist.
Is it the case that in the border regions— wherever they may be— there is no living of the holy life among the barbarians who do not understand,
where there is no access for bhikkhus, bhikkhunīs, upāsakas, or upāsikās;
whereas in the Middle Countries— wherever they may be— there is the living of the holy life, and wherever it may not be?
It should not be said so.
Is it the case that among human beings there are places where the holy life can be lived and places where it cannot?
Yes, it is.
Where does it exist, and where does it not exist?

It does not exist in the border regions among the barbarians who are ignorant, where there is no movement of monks, nuns, laymen, or laywomen; it exists in the Middle Countries, where the holy life is lived.

Is it not the case that in the bordering regions, among the barbarians who are unintelligent, there is no living of the holy life (brahmacariya)—wherein there is no going for monks, nuns, laymen, or laywomen?
Yes, it is.
Is it then not the case that in the Middle Countries there is no living of the holy life?
It should not be said so.
Is there a living of the holy life (brahmacariya) in the Middle Countries? Yes.
Is there a dwelling in the holy life among the border regions, among the barbarians who do not understand, where there is no access for bhikkhus, bhikkhunīs, upāsakas, or upāsikās?
One should certainly not say so.
Is there a dwelling in the holy life among the devas?
“Yes, [they do].
“But was it not said by the Blessed One:
‘Monks, in three respects the people of Jambudīpa surpass the people of Uttarakuru and the gods of the Tāvatiṃsa heaven’?”
"By which three?
By being brave, by possessing mindfulness, and by dwelling here in the holy life.
Is this indeed a sutta?
“Yes, [it is so].
“In that case, there is no living the holy life among the devas.
This was said by the Blessed One at Sāvatthī.
“Is it the case that ‘herein lies the living of the holy life’?”—
“Yes.”—
“Then does the living of the holy life exist only in Sāvatthī, and not elsewhere?”
It should not be said so.

When a person who is a non-returner has abandoned the five lower fetters but has not yet abandoned the five higher fetters, where does the fruit arise for him after passing away from here and being reborn there?
Right there.

If, for a person who is a non-returner (anāgāmī), the five lower fetters (orambhāgiya-saṃyojana) have been abandoned while the five higher fetters (uddhambhāgiya-saṃyojana) have not yet been abandoned, such that upon passing away from here and being reborn there, the fruit arises in that very place;
then indeed, you must not say:
"There is no living of the holy life (brahmacariya) among the devas."

For a person who is a non-returner (*anāgāmī*), the five lower fetters (*orambhāgiya-saṃyojana*) have been abandoned, but the five higher fetters (*uddhambhāgiya-saṃyojana*) have not yet been abandoned.
When such a person passes away from here and is reborn there, where is the bearing of the burden, where is the full understanding of suffering,
where is the abandoning of defilements, where is the realization of cessation, and where is the penetration of the unshakable?
In that very case:

if, for a person who is a non-returner (*anāgāmī*), the five lower fetters (*orambhāgiya-saṃyojana*) have been abandoned, while the five higher fetters (*uddhambhāgiya-saṃyojana*) have not yet been abandoned, such that upon passing away from here and being reborn there, he attains the penetration of the unshakable (*akuppapaṭivedha*);
then indeed, you should not say this.
“There is no dwelling in the holy life among the devas.
For a person who is a non-returner (anāgāmī), the five lower fetters (orambhāgiya-saṃyojana) have been abandoned, while the five higher fetters (uddhambhāgiya-saṃyojana) have not yet been abandoned;
having passed away from here and reappeared there, the fruit arises there, and the burden is carried there.
In that case, there is the full understanding of suffering, there is the abandoning of defilements, there is the realization of cessation, and there is the penetration of the unshakable;
in what sense do you say,
"There is no living of the holy life among the devas"?
Indeed, it is so: a person who is a non-returner realizes the fruit there by means of the path developed here.
This concludes the discourse on the connection regarding the holy life.
Is it the case that a person who is a non-returner realizes the fruit there by means of the path developed here?
“Yes,” you say.
“Does a person who is a stream-enterer realize the fruit here in this life by means of the path developed there?
You should not say so.
Is it the case that a person who is a non-returner realizes the fruit there by means of a path developed here? Yes.
Is it the case that a person who is a once-returner, or a person who attains final nibbāna here, realizes the fruit here by means of a path developed there?
It should not be said so.
Is it the case that a person who is a stream-enterer realizes the fruit here by means of a path developed here? Yes.
Is it not the case that one should not say: "An *anāgāmī* person realizes the fruit there by means of the path developed there"?
Is it not the case that one should say: "A *sakadāgāmī* person, or a person who attains final nibbāna here, realizes the fruit here by means of the path developed here"?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Does a person who is a non-returner realize the fruit there by means of the path developed there?
You should not say so… [and so on]…
Is it the case that for a person who has reached the goal here and now, the path is being cultivated but the defilements are not abandoned? Yes.
Is it the case that for a person practicing for the realization of the fruit of stream-entry, the path is being cultivated but the defilements are not abandoned?
It should not be said so… [as before]… Here,
for a person who has attained finality while still living, is it the case that the path is cultivated but the defilements are not abandoned?
Yes, it is.
Is it the case that for a person practicing for the realization of the fruit of once-returning …pe… for a person practicing for the realization of arhatship,
the path is being cultivated but the defilements are not abandoned?
One should certainly not say so …pe….
Is it the case that for a person practicing for the realization of the fruit of stream-entry, the path is cultivated and the defilements are abandoned simultaneously, neither before nor after?
Yes. Is it then the case that for a person who has attained final liberation here and now, the path is cultivated and the defilements are abandoned simultaneously, neither before nor after?
It should not be said so.
Is it the case that for a person practicing for the realization of the fruit of once-returning …pe… for a person practicing for the realization of arhatship,
the path is cultivated and defilements are abandoned simultaneously, neither before nor after?
“Yes,” you say.
“In this case, for a person who has reached the goal after leaving this world, is it the case that the path is cultivated and the defilements are abandoned neither before nor after [simultaneously]?
You must not say so.
Is it the case that a person who is a non-returner—one who has done what was to be done and developed what was to be developed—is reborn there?
Yes. Is an arahant reborn there? No.
It should not be said so.
[Is it the case that] an arahant is reborn? Yes.
Is there a further becoming for an arahant?
One should not say so.
Is there a further becoming for an arahant? One should not say so.
“Yes,” [you say].
“Does an Arahant go from existence to existence, go from destiny to destiny, go from saṃsāra to saṃsāra, go from rebirth to rebirth?
You should not speak thus.
Is it the case that a person who is a non-returner—one who has done what was to be done, developed what was to be developed, and laid down the burden—is reborn there?
Yes. Does he then develop the path again for the sake of bearing that burden? No.
It should not be said so.

Is it the case that a non-returner (anāgāmī) person—one who has done what was to be done, developed what was to be developed, yet has not fully understood suffering, has not abandoned the defilements, has not realized cessation, and has not penetrated the unshakable—reborn there?
Yes, it is.
Does one further develop the path for the penetration of the unshakable?
One should not say so.

Is it not the case that a person who is a non-returner—one who has done what was to be done, developed what was to be developed, and laid down the burden—arises there [in the higher realms] and does not further develop the path for the removal of the burden?
“Yes,” you say.
“And does one who has not yet laid down the burden attain final nibbāna there?
You must not say so.

Is it the case that a person who is a non-returner—one who has done what was to be done, developed what was to be developed, but has not fully understood suffering, has not abandoned the defilements, has not realized cessation, and has not penetrated the unshakable—arises there [in the Pure Abodes] and does not further develop the path for the penetration of the unshakable?
Yes. And does he attain final nibbāna there without having penetrated the unshakable? Yes.
It should not be said thus:
"Just as a deer pierced by an arrow dies after traveling a great distance, so too does a non-returner (anāgāmī) person realize the fruit there by means of the path developed here.

Is it then the case that, just as a deer pierced by an arrow dies with the arrow still within it after traveling a great distance, so too does a non-returner person attain final nibbāna there with the arrow still within him by means of the path developed here?
It should not be stated thus… [as before]… The Discussion on the Holy Life is finished.
